audit.whatIsWrong: The whole content layer described a champion that no longer exists. It named 'Starsurge', 'Voice of Light' and 'Comet of Legend' — none of which are in Aurelion Sol's kit — across whys[2], whys[4], whys[5], all four spikes, mid, late, wants.you[1], wants.foe[0], wants.foe[1] and wants.foe[2]. The packet's defect list flags the same thing from the other side: the page never names a real ability.
audit.why: His actual abilities are Cosmic Creator (P, Stardust that permanently improves each ability), Breath of Light (Q, 3s, 750, a channel), Astral Flight (W, 22/20.5/19/17.5/16s, 1500, a channel that flies over terrain), Singularity (E, 12s, 750, black hole that pulls and executes at the centre below a percent of health), and Falling Star / The Skies Descend (R, 120/110/100s, 1250, stun).
audit.corrected: Every fabricated name replaced with the real ability and its real numbers, and the two decisive interactions written in: both Q and W are channels any CC cancels, and Astral Flight flies OVER terrain so Crystallize does not stop him.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers gave different owners on six of seven rows. Full: Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Anivia/Skill/Aurelion Sol. Content and packet: Anivia x5 / Aurelion Sol / Anivia.
audit.why: Anivia holds the early lane on range and on the channel interaction — Flash Frost is 1075 against a 750 Breath of Light he has to stand still to hold, and Astral Flight does not arrive until 3. The first-item row goes to Sol because stacked Stardust turns Singularity into a percent-health execute. The final row returns to Anivia's zone control.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side to Anivia, phases[5].side to Aurelion Sol, phases[6].side to Anivia; early ratings raised to 6/10; every phases[N].why rewritten to match its new owner and to name real abilities.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] pinned Anivia's first-item spike to Rylai's, against the full layer's own itemization, and none of the spikes carried a real cooldown.
audit.why: Anivia's first-item spike is mana and storm uptime. Sol's spikes are Astral Flight at 3 (22s at rank 1), Falling Star at 6 (120s at rank 1), and Stardust accumulation, which is a continuous spike rather than a level.
audit.corrected: spikes[0..3] rebuilt on real numbers and on Stardust scaling.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns gave no numbers and described Astral Flight only as 'his reposition and escape'.
audit.why: Astral Flight 22/20.5/19/17.5/16s, Singularity 12s, Breath of Light 3s (and no cooldown at all while he is flying), Falling Star 120/110/100s.
audit.corrected: Numbers written in, along with the two facts that change how you use them: the flight crosses terrain, and both it and the breath are channels.
sources: kit cooldown strings and W text

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly told the player to wall him off. Crystallize is the one tool that does not work here.
audit.why: Astral Flight's text is 'flies over terrain in a targeted direction'. Anivia has no dash, and _missing carries the matching rule: he can cut your retreat with Astral Flight while you cannot follow.
audit.corrected: Wall advice replaced with stun-the-channel advice in winCon, breakdown.late, dontsFull[1], report[5] and late; the retreat-cutting risk written into wants.foe[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Singularity's execute threshold was never mentioned anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Riot's text: the centre of the black hole executes enemies below a certain percentage of health, and the ability grants Stardust for each second a champion is caught inside. The kit carries both percentHealth and execute flags.
audit.corrected: Written into tradeBad, dontsFull[2], breakdown.feeding, whys[5], spikes[3] and late as a health-number rule rather than a health-bar one.
sources: enemy kit E text and flags

notes: This matchup's content layer was written against the pre-rework Aurelion Sol and named three abilities that do not exist (Starsurge, Voice of Light, Comet of Legend). Every one has been replaced. The single most important correction is that Crystallize does NOT stop him: Astral Flight flies over terrain, which inverts the advice the page gave in five places. Whether Flash Frost's stun cancels Falling Star, and whether Singularity's pull can drag Anivia's egg, are not answerable from the kit data and were not asserted. The exact Stardust threshold that upgrades Falling Star into The Skies Descend is truncated in the kit text and was left unquantified.
